close_reason: Shipped via PR #1 squash c37cf5a. Windows Python environment discipline landed at operating-disciplines.md §13 (PYTHONUTF8=1 for per-script invocations + per-machine setx PYTHONUTF8 1 noted as PRINCIPAL responsibility).
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-07 by PRINCIPAL during Batch G xft.7 quality cluster work. Pattern: agent-authored helper Python scripts repeatedly crash on Windows with cp1252 codec errors when output contains non-ASCII characters (Greek theta in PDFs, em-dashes in print statements, etc.).

The ariadne--sh7 fix reconfigured sys.stdout in ariadne CLI's main() entry. That works for the CLI binary but does NOT cover the broader case: ad-hoc Python scripts written by PLINY/VERA/ADA/etc. during gauntlet runs on Windows machines have their own stdout that is cp1252 by default. Every helper script that prints non-ASCII content crashes.

This is a per-machine environmental issue with two complementary fixes:

(1) User-level: set PYTHONUTF8=1 globally in the user environment (Windows: setx PYTHONUTF8 1). One-time per machine. Covers every Python script. PRINCIPAL handles their own machine via this approach; substrate cannot do this for them.

(2) Substrate-level: operating-disciplines.md gets a Windows-Python-environment subsection that says: when invoking Python scripts on Windows (detected via os.name == 'nt' or PRINCIPAL-flagged Windows deployment), agents should set PYTHONUTF8=1 in the bash environment for the invocation, OR include sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8') at the top of any helper script.

Recommended: ship both. (1) is the cheapest fix; (2) is the durable substrate that protects future deployments where (1) hasn't been applied.

Where in substrate: new subsection under operating-disciplines.md (likely §4 disciplines or a new top-level after §11 autonomous-mode-setup checklist). Names the rule + the empirical anchor (sh7 + the recurring smoke-helper failures during Batch C/D/F/G).

Empirical anchor: Batch G smoke #1 Test 3 crashed on cp1252 (em-dash in PLINY's smoke probe print statement). Same root cause as sh7. The pattern has surfaced repeatedly across the xft.7 quality cluster work — this filing captures the systemic fix at the substrate layer.

Out of scope: substrate auto-detection of OS (the role files are just instructions; bash invocations either set the var or they don't).

Empirical lineage: sh7 (Batch A) fixed the CLI-binary case; Batch G surfaced the helper-script case as a related-but-distinct manifestation. Both are now durable: sh7 in code, this ticket in substrate.
title: operating-disciplines.md: Windows Python environment — set PYTHONUTF8=1 for every Python invocation
